---
title: "Who Lives Where in Sarasota County"
subtitle: "A neighborhood-by-neighborhood look at race and ethnicity, using US Census Bureau data"
author: "Zheyre Tolliver, ISC2076, New College of Florida"
date: today
date-format: "MMMM D, YYYY"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
---

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)

sarasota <- read_rds("sarasota.rds")

county <- sarasota |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  summarize(total = sum(estimate), pop = sum(summary_est), .by = variable) |>
  mutate(share = 100 * total / pop)

pct <- function(g) round(county$share[county$variable == g])

map_group <- function(g, color) {
  sarasota |>
    filter(variable == g) |>
    ggplot(aes(fill = percent)) +
    geom_sf(color = "white", linewidth = 0.08) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f6f1fb", high = color,
                        labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)) +
    labs(fill = "Share of\nresidents",
         caption = "Source: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2019 to 2023") +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.title = element_text(color = "#4a3a5c"),
          legend.text = element_text(color = "#6b5a7e"),
          plot.caption = element_text(color = "#8a7a9a", size = 9))
}
```

::: {.keyfacts}
**At a glance:** Across Sarasota County, about **`r pct("White")`%** of residents identify as White (non-Hispanic), **`r pct("Hispanic")`%** as Hispanic, **`r pct("Black")`%** as Black, and **`r pct("Asian")`%** as Asian.
:::

Sarasota County looks very different depending on which neighborhood you stand in. Using the Census Bureau's most recent five-year survey, these maps break the county into census tracts, small areas of a few thousand residents each, and show where each group makes up a larger or smaller share of the population.

## White residents

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
map_group("White", "#4a2c6b")
```

White residents are the majority in most of the county, which is why this map is dark almost everywhere. Lighter tracts mark the neighborhoods where other groups make up a bigger share.

## Hispanic residents

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
map_group("Hispanic", "#7b4fa6")
```

Hispanic residents make up about `r pct("Hispanic")`% of the county, but they are not spread evenly. Darker tracts show the neighborhoods where Hispanic residents are concentrated.

## Black residents

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
map_group("Black", "#5b3a80")
```

Black residents are about `r pct("Black")`% of the county overall, yet a few tracts stand out sharply. These include parts of the city of Sarasota, home to the historic Newtown community.

## Asian residents

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
map_group("Asian", "#9b6fc9")
```

Asian residents are the smallest of the four groups, at about `r pct("Asian")`% of the county, with modest concentrations in a handful of tracts.

::: {.methods}
**About the data:** Figures come from the US Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2019 to 2023 five-year estimates), table B03002, downloaded with the tidycensus package in R. "White," "Black," and "Asian" refer to non-Hispanic residents; Hispanic residents can be of any race. Survey estimates have margins of error, which are larger for small tracts.
:::
